//: Edits Kimochi makes to an extension's files as it serves them (src-tauri/src/extensions.rs and,
for the dev server, scripts/extension-patches.mjs). Keep these to a minimum: each is a single
exact `find` that must occur once in the pinned file; a file where it does not is served
unpatched and the host falls back to its older path. `requires` names what the replacement
calls inside the file, so an upstream rename is caught by scripts/extension-patches.test.mjs
before it ships, and the engine contract suite (npm run test:engines) checks the result in a
real browser. Run both after moving a pin (scripts/sync-extension.mjs).

patches.why: Read along looks a word up by its place in the text, the way a hover there would, with no pointer events, key presses or selection (host/ext/content.js lookupText). Hachidori exposes only scanSelectedText, which needs a selection. kimochiClear empties the pop-up as the next word's answer arrives, through the pop-up's own clear: Hachidori would otherwise restyle and lay out the last word's entries once more before replacing them, which doubled each step's time on a Steam Deck. It answers whether Hachidori will still draw that answer: a lookup it dropped meanwhile (a window blur cancels one in flight) is asked for again, and its pop-up is not left emptied.
patches.replace: const reader = Object.freeze({ scanSelectedText, kimochiLookupAt(node, offset) { if (disposed || !options.hoverEnabled || !node) return false; const candidate = resolveCandidateAt(node, offset); if (!candidate) return false; clearScanTimer(); cancelScanDwell(); clearHideTimer(); activeSelectionCandidate = null; lookupCandidate(candidate); return true; }, kimochiClear() { if (disposed || !pendingCandidateLookup || pendingCandidateLookup.token !== rootLevel.lookupToken) return false; if (rootLevel.popup && !rootLevel.popup.hidden) rootLevel.view?.clear(); return true; } });

patches.why: 10ten ignores a pointer move with a modifier held at the same point as the last one, in Safari (isSafari(), which WebKitGTK's user agent also matches), to dodge a WebKit bug fixed in May 2023 (WebKit/WebKit#14221). Every WebKit Kimochi runs on has the fix. Kimochi's Shift scan sends exactly such a move: on Wayland the overlay has no keyboard, so pressing Shift over a stationary pointer re-sends the move at the same point with shiftKey set (host/linux-scan-input.js), and 10ten dropped it, never looking the word up.

Moving from word to word, a pop-up drawn with only its first entry, then filled a frame or two later, flashes nearly empty when that entry is short (a name, a particle): the pop-up keeps its size, so the frame between two full ones is mostly blank. The renderer takes how many entries to draw before the first paint (render/popup.js `initialResultCount`, 1 unless given); three fill what the pop-up shows in one frame, and the rest still follow as before. It adds a few milliseconds to a lookup that already shows in single digits.

With hachidori-first-view-count: the entries drawn before the first paint get their glossaries then too, rather than an entry header over an empty body for a frame. Hachidori fills only the first entry at once and the rest on the next task, since only the first used to be drawn.
